passages.text: You will not otherwise endure undertaking the great effort needed for your cleansing unless you become angry with yourselves and rebuke yourselves for the ways in which, like useless servants, you were ambushed by agreeing with your evil desires. Then you will be able to apply your righteous anger to your mind like fire to a field left uncultivated. So if you do not have righteous fire—I mean anger against evil desires—learn what good things you have been ambushed and deprived of, what punishment you have been prepared for, and by whom you have been deceived. In this way your mind, becoming clear-minded and kindled to anger like fire by the teaching of the one who sent us, may be able to consume the things that are against desire. Believe me: if you are willing, you will be able to set everything right.

lexical_decisions.chosen: like useless servants
lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses the POB servant gloss; the comparison retains the underlying bonded-status and master-accountability sense of δοῦλοι.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὰ κατὰ τῆς ἐπιθυμίας ἀναλῶσαι δυνηθῇ.
lexical_decisions.chosen: may be able to consume the things that are against desire.
lexical_decisions.rationale: τὰ substantivizes the following prepositional phrase, and κατά with the supplied genitive τῆς naturally means against. The formal grouping preserves that syntax without silently replacing the genitive with an accusative or moving opposition to qualify the consuming action. Its precise intended sense remains difficult in the surrounding fire-and-desire argument; things belonging to desire would require a textual or syntactic account not established by this wording.

source_issues.source_quote: τὰ κατὰ τῆς ἐπιθυμίας ἀναλῶσαι δυνηθῇ.
source_issues.issue: The formal grouping the things that are against desire is defensible from the supplied article and genitive construction, but its fit with the surrounding fire-and-desire argument is difficult. This translation does not claim to resolve that difficulty or emend the Greek. The previous adverbial attachment is not retained, because an independent object for τὰ was not adequately established.

passages.text: “But from the beginning he ought to have made us not even think about such things at all.” In saying this, you do not know what freedom of choice is or how it is possible to be truly good. For the person who is good by his own choice is truly good; the person made good by someone else’s compulsion is not truly so, because he is not what he is by his own choice. Since each person’s freedom produces what is truly good and reveals what is truly evil, God has arranged, through the circumstances, for becoming an enemy or a friend to lie within each person. “No,” someone says, “rather, he himself makes us think everything that we think.” Stop! What further blasphemy are you speaking when you say this? For if, in everything we may think, we are moved by him, you are calling him the cause of sexual immoralities, shameless acts, greed, and every blasphemy. Stop speaking ill of him, you who ought to speak well of him and assign him every honor. And do not say, “God does not claim honor.” Even if he claims nothing, we still ought, with an eye to what is just, to repay with a thankful voice the one who has benefited us in every way.

lexical_decisions.chosen: freedom of choice
lexical_decisions.rationale: Literally self-determination or being in one’s own power; the paragraph explicitly contrasts personal choice and external compulsion.

lexical_decisions.chosen: through the circumstances
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὑποθέσεις can denote situations, underlying conditions, or proposed matters; circumstances fits the arrangements in which choice operates without specifying their exact mechanism.

lexical_decisions.chosen: sexual immoralities, shameless acts, greed
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves distinct vice categories without embellishing sexual content or reducing all three to a generic evil.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: εἰ γὰρ πᾶν ὅ,τι ἂν ἐνθυμηθῶμεν, ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ἐνεργούμεθα
lexical_decisions.chosen: For if, in everything we may think, we are moved by him
lexical_decisions.rationale: We remains the subject of ἐνεργούμεθα. Moved or actuated concerns the alleged divine agency in our thinking; it does not make thoughts into actions implemented by God.

passages.text: For even if you escape punishment through the dissolution of the body, how will you be able through destruction to escape your soul, which is indestructible? For even the soul of the impious is immortal; it would have been better for them not to have it indestructible. Punished by unquenchable fire with unending punishment and not dying, it cannot come to an end, to its own hurt. But perhaps one of you will say, “You frighten us, Peter.” Then teach us how we are to state things as they are while remaining silent, for we cannot make them known to you otherwise. If we remain silent, you are ambushed by evils through ignorance; if we speak, we are suspected of frightening you on a false premise. How, then, are we to deal with the evil lurking within you and cunningly sowing in you notions hostile to God under the pretext of friendship with God? Be reconciled with yourselves: taking refuge in him with good deeds is for your salvation. There is within you an irrational desire hostile to God; for through supposed understanding, it strengthens ignorance.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῷ εἰς τὴν ὑμετέραν κακῷ ἐνδομυχοῦντι
lexical_decisions.chosen: the evil lurking within you
lexical_decisions.rationale: The possessive phrase τὴν ὑμετέραν has no expressed feminine noun in the supplied wording. Within you preserves the contextual location of the lurking evil without inventing a named organ or restoring Greek words.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἐπὶ κακῷ τῷ αὐτῆς τέλος λαβεῖν οὐκ ἔχει.
lexical_decisions.chosen: it cannot come to an end, to its own hurt
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains endless survival as harmful to the punished soul; the author’s claim is not harmonized with annihilation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ πανούργως ὑποσπείροντι ὑμῖν τὰς θεῷ ἐχθραινούσας ὑπονοίας
lexical_decisions.chosen: and cunningly sowing in you notions hostile to God
lexical_decisions.rationale: In you explicitly preserves ὑμῖν as the recipients of the sowing, separately from the earlier location of the lurking evil.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὑπονοίᾳ γὰρ φρονήσεως τὴν ἄγνοιαν κρατύνει.
lexical_decisions.chosen: for through supposed understanding, it strengthens ignorance.
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὑπόνοια is a supposition, notion, or suspicion; supposed understanding preserves that cognitive claim rather than introducing a deliberate display or pretension. For retains the explanatory γάρ.

passages.text: Others say, “God has not cared about us.” This too is false. For if he truly did not care, he would not make his sun rise on good and evil people or send his rain on the righteous and unrighteous. Others say, “We are more reverent because we revere both him and the statues.” I do not think so—if someone who says this tells a king, “I assign you the same honor as I do the dead and discarded dung,” I do not think he will come off well. But someone will say, “Do you call our objects of reverence dung?” Yes, I say. For you made them useless to yourselves by counting them among objects of worship, although their substance might have served some other purpose, even the use of dung. But now it is not useful even for this, since you have reshaped it and worship it. How can you, the most impious of all, also claim to be more reverent? For this one incomparable sin alone you truly owe the destruction of your soul, if you persist. Just as a son who receives many benefits from his father and gives someone else, who is not his father, the honor owed to his father certainly becomes disinherited, so, when he lives according to his father’s judgment and gives thanks for the benefits, he reasonably becomes an heir.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῆς οὐσίας αὐτῶν ἴσως εἰς ἄλλο τι (εἰς χρῆσιν κόπρου) εὐχρηστησάσης.
lexical_decisions.chosen: although their substance might have served some other purpose, even the use of dung
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the parenthetical comparison with useful dung rather than upgrading the idols into useful objects of worship.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ταύτῃ αὐτῇ τῇ μιᾷ καὶ ἀσυγκρίτῳ ἀμαρτίᾳ ψυχῆς ὄλεθρον ὀφείλοντες
lexical_decisions.chosen: For this one incomparable sin alone you truly owe the destruction of your soul
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the severe stated consequence, with the following if-you-persist condition retained in the main text.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐκ οἶμαι, εἰ τοῦτο λέγων τις ἐρεῖ βασιλεῖ Τὴν ἴσην σοι ἀπονέμω τιμήν, οἵαν καὶ τοῖς νεκροῖς καὶ τῇ ἐρριμμένῃ κοπρίᾳ· οὐκ οἴομαι εἰ καλῶς ἀπαλλάξει.
lexical_decisions.chosen: I do not think so—if ... I do not think he will come off well.
lexical_decisions.rationale: The selected edition repeats the negative assertion οὐκ οἶμαι / οὐκ οἴομαι around a conditional and syntactic restart. Both assertions remain, rather than being compressed into one; the restart is a supplied feature, not alleged OCR corruption.

passages.text: Others say, “We shall be acting impiously if we abandon the objects of reverence handed down to us from our fathers, for it is like keeping something entrusted to us.” By this reasoning, then, even if someone is the child of a robber, or of a father, or of a man who lives shamefully, is the son, once he has become clear-minded, not to choose the better course, lest he act impiously and sin by not doing the same things as his parents? How senseless are those who say, “We worship these things so as not to trouble him himself,” as though God were troubled by being praised but not troubled by being blasphemed through ingratitude! Why, then, when rain is withheld, do you look to heaven for everything and offer prayers and entreaties? And when you succeed, why do you forget so quickly? For after reaping or gathering the vintage, you immediately assign the firstfruits to idols that are nothing, quickly forgetting the God who did you good. Then you go into sacred groves and temples and feast while performing sacrifices. For this reason some of you say, “These things have been well devised for comfort and feasting.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: κἂν λῃστοῦ τις ἢ πατρὸς ἢ αἰσχροβίου
lexical_decisions.chosen: even if someone is the child of a robber, or of a father, or of a man who lives shamefully
lexical_decisions.rationale: Both printed ἢ disjunctions remain. The child relationship is inferred from the ensuing explicit son, not restored from missing text; the redundant father remains the supplied reading. Taking the first ἢ as conjectural ᾖ would create a smoother alternative, but that conjecture is not adopted.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐκ ὀφείλει ὁ υἱὸς νήψας τὸ κρεῖττον ἑλέσθαι, ἵνα μὴ ἀσεβήσῃ καὶ μὴ τὰ ἴσα τοῖς γονεῦσιν ποιῶν ἀμαρτάνῃ;
lexical_decisions.chosen: is the son, once he has become clear-minded, not to choose the better course, lest ...?
lexical_decisions.rationale: Once clear-minded keeps νήψας circumstantial, not a second commanded action. Under by this reasoning, the question tests the proposed obligation to preserve ancestral practices and its consequence for choosing better. Is not obliged to choose is another rendering of οὐκ ὀφείλει; is not to choose makes the reductio consequence explicit without presenting it as Peter’s own counsel.

lexical_decisions.chosen: look to heaven for everything
lexical_decisions.rationale: The neuter accusative τὰ πάντα qualifies the scope of looking, not the nominative people looking. Looking wholly toward heaven is another viable adverbial rendering; for everything is selected in the petition-for-rain context.

passages.text: Senseless people, become just judges of what is being said. For even if one ought to give oneself over to bodily enjoyment here, which feast is better: one by rivers and woods and groves, where there are banquets and drinking parties and shaded places, or one where there is the frenzy of demons, cutting of hands, cutting off of genitals, fits of fury and madness, clipping of hair, boasts, possession, shrieks, and all those things done theatrically to astound the senseless, so that you offer their owed prayers and thanksgivings to things deader even than the dead?

lexical_decisions.chosen: cutting of hands, cutting off of genitals
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves both named ritual injuries soberly without euphemism or added detail.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to things deader even than the dead
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the pointed comparative and its rhetorical excess.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅπως τὰς αὐτῶν ὀφειλομένας εὐχὰς καὶ εὐχαριστίας καὶ νεκρῶν νεκροτέροις προσενέγκητε;
lexical_decisions.chosen: so that you offer their owed prayers and thanksgivings to things deader even than the dead?
lexical_decisions.rationale: Their preserves the printed third-person αὐτῶν alongside second-person you offer. It can refer to the previously mentioned senseless people, potentially including the audience. Your is a contextual identification alternative, but the main text does not silently harmonize the pronouns.

passages.text: And why do you do these things gladly? Since the serpent nesting within you, who sowed fruitless desire in you, does not want to tell you, I will remind you by explaining. It is like this: in the worship of God it is proclaimed that one must be clear-minded, exercise self-control, master anger, not appropriate what belongs to others, live justly, reasonably, steadily, and gently, and discipline oneself in deprivation rather than, when lacking something, take it unjustly from someone else and be filled. But among the so-called gods, the opposite happens. Some commands are also given to inspire awe at righteousness; yet even if you perform all the commands, ignorance of God alone is sufficient for your punishment. Nevertheless, you gather at the places you have assigned to them, gladly become drunk, and kindle altars. Their drifting sacrificial smoke, through the power, brings even the blind and deaf spirits to the place where they smell it. Thus, of those there, some are filled with possession, others with strange foods, while others turn to shameless conduct and others to thefts and murders. For the vapor of the blood there and the libation of wines set even the impure spirits themselves dancing. Lurking within you, they make you take pleasure in what goes on there, surround you through dreams with false visions, and punish you with countless afflictions. For under the pretext of the so-called sacrificial offerings you are filled with fierce demons, who also kill you while cunningly escaping your notice, so that you do not understand the plot against you. For under the pretext of some abuse, necessity, passion, anger, or grief, they remove you from life by hanging, by drowning you in water, by throwing you from a cliff, by your own hand, by a stroke, or by some other affliction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ ἔνια εἰς κατάπληξιν δικαιοσύνης παραγγέλλεται
lexical_decisions.chosen: Some commands are also given to inspire awe at righteousness
lexical_decisions.rationale: The phrase relates certain commands to an impressive effect associated with righteousness. An impressive display of righteousness is another viable rendering; the main text does not decide that all such commands are merely fraudulent.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἡ κνίσα ῥεμβομένη καὶ τὰ τυφλὰ καὶ κωφὰ πνεύματα διὰ τῆς ἐξουσίας ἄγει εἰς τὸν τῆς ὀσφρήσεως αὐτῶν τόπον.
lexical_decisions.chosen: Their drifting sacrificial smoke, through the power, brings even the blind and deaf spirits to the place where they smell it.
lexical_decisions.rationale: Smoke is the grammatical subject, but the possessor or source of ἐξουσία is not stated. The power leaves it unspecified. Its power, assigning power to the smoke, is a defensible contextual alternative, not an explicit Greek possessive. No divine or demonic source of the power is independently added.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ αὐτὰ χοροῖ τὰ ἀκάθαρτα πνεύματα
lexical_decisions.chosen: set even the impure spirits themselves dancing
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the dancing image, not merely attraction.

lexical_decisions.chosen: by your own hand, by a stroke
lexical_decisions.rationale: By your own hand understands the demons as inducing the victims’ self-killing, supported by the listed pretexts and means of death. αὐτοχειρία can also be killing with one’s own hand, so direct killing by the demons themselves is a material alternative given the surrounding demonic subjects. Stroke preserves the separate ἀποπληξία without adding clinical detail.

passages.text: Therefore the prophet of truth, knowing that the world was greatly deceived and seeing that it had agreed with evil, did not love peace with it, since that peace arose from error. Setting out that it ultimately brings death upon all who agree with evil, in place of error he cast into those who had become clear-minded an anger against the one who had ambushed them, like fire and resembling a sword. Holding out the word, he does away with ignorance through knowledge, as though cutting and separating the living from the dead. So, as evil was overcome by knowledge in accordance with the law, war gripped everything. For the sake of salvation a son who yielded separated from a disobedient father, or a father from a child, or a mother from a daughter, or a daughter from a mother—in short, relatives from relatives and friends from companions.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅτι εἰς τέλος ἐπιφέρει πᾶσιν τοῖς πρὸς κακίαν ὁμογνωμονοῦσιν παραθεὶς
lexical_decisions.chosen: Setting out that it ultimately brings death upon all who agree with evil
lexical_decisions.rationale: The object brought is implicit. Death is inferred from the end of 11.18 and the ensuing living/dead contrast. The it can be the peace founded on error or its sustaining error; no new punishment is specified.

lexical_decisions.chosen: a son who yielded
lexical_decisions.rationale: The recipient of yielding is not explicit. The saving instruction is contextual, but the English does not insert that recipient.

source_issues.source_quote: ὅτι εἰς τέλος ἐπιφέρει πᾶσιν τοῖς πρὸς κακίαν ὁμογνωμονοῦσιν παραθεὶς
source_issues.issue: The object of brings upon is implicit. Death in the main text is inferred from the immediately preceding death-language and ensuing living/dead contrast. The antecedent can be error-based peace or its sustaining error.

The selected, image-checked edition prints a period between the article τῶν and noun νεκρῶν. English reads them together as from the dead despite this intervening punctuation. This is a supplied print feature, not assumed OCR corruption; no replacement Greek has been introduced.

passages.text: And let no one say, “How is this just, for parents to be separated from children and children from parents?” It is entirely just. For if by staying with them they not only did them no good but also perished with them, how is it not just for the one who wants to be saved to be separated from the one who does not want to be saved but wants to perish together? Moreover, those who had understood what is better did not themselves want to be separated, but to remain with them and benefit them by teaching better things. Therefore the disobedient, unwilling to listen to them, themselves fought against them, separating them, persecuting them, and hating them. But those who suffered these things pitied them as people ambushed by ignorance and, taught to understand, prayed for those who mistreated them, having learned that ignorance is the cause of sin. For the teacher himself, when nailed up, prayed to the Father that the sin of those killing him might be forgiven, saying, “Father, forgive them their sins, for they do not know what they are doing.” Becoming imitators of the teacher themselves, in their sufferings they prayed for those who inflicted them, as they had been taught. Thus they did not separate because they hated their parents, since they even offered prayers for those who were not their parents but had become enemies, and try to love them as they were commanded.

lexical_decisions.chosen: taught to understand
lexical_decisions.rationale: The dative connects instruction in understanding with the prayerful response, not with a newly supplied revelation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: they ... separate
lexical_decisions.rationale: Bracketed letters are already supplied by the selected edition; no new restoration has been made.

lexical_decisions.chosen: who were not their parents
lexical_decisions.rationale: Follows the supplied bracketed reading and preserves the contrast with enemies.

lexical_decisions.chosen: when nailed up
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the physical nail-language.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀπὸ τοῦ μὴ θέλοντος, συναπολέσθαι δὲ βουλομένου;
lexical_decisions.chosen: from the one who does not want to be saved but wants to perish together?
lexical_decisions.rationale: The person described by βουλομένου remains the subject of co-perishing. To be saved repeats the contextual object of willing in the prior clause, not a new wish for other people’s destruction.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅθεν οἱ ἀπειθεῖς ἐπακούειν αὐτῶν μὴ θέλοντες αὐτοὶ αὐτοὺς ἐπολέμουν, χωρίζοντες, διώκοντες, μισοῦντες.
lexical_decisions.chosen: themselves fought against them, separating them, persecuting them, and hating them.
lexical_decisions.rationale: The expressed αὐτούς is taken as the shared object of the parallel participles, giving the disobedient people agency in imposing separation. Separating from them is an intransitive alternative, but it is less source-transparent after the statement that the instructed people did not want separation.

passages.text: But tell me: how do you love your parents? If you do so with a constant regard for what is just, I join in your prayer; but if merely as it happens, I do not, for even on a small pretext you can become their enemies. If you love with knowledge, tell us what “parents” means. You will say, “Founders of a family line.” Why, then, have you not loved the origin of all things, if you have undertaken to do this with a just mind? But even now you will say, “We have not seen him.” Why, then, do you flatter insensible things without having searched? And what of this? Even if it was difficult for you to know what God is, you could not fail to know what is not God, so that you might reason that God is not wood, not stone, not bronze, or anything else made of perishable matter.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the origin of all things
lexical_decisions.rationale: γένος links the argument to lineage and parentage. Origin or source here refers to God; progenitor of all is a viable more explicitly personal alternative.

lexical_decisions.chosen: I join in your prayer
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the prayer compound; join in wishing this is also possible, rather than bare agreement.

lexical_decisions.chosen: And what of this?
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the separate rhetorical question introducing the final argument.

passages.text: Were they not shaped on a lathe by iron—and was not the iron that shaped them on a lathe softened by fire—and is not fire itself extinguished by water? Does not water get its motion from wind, and does not wind have the origin of its movement from the God who made all things? For this is what the prophet Moses said: “In the beginning God made heaven and earth. But the earth was invisible and unformed, and darkness was over the abyss, and God’s Spirit was borne over the water.” And when God speaks, this Spirit, like his hand, fashions everything, separating light from darkness and spreading out the visible heaven after the invisible one, so that the regions above may be inhabited by the angels of light, while those below may be administered by the human being together with all things made for his sake.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ δὲ ὕδωρ οὐχ ὑπὸ πνεύματος τὴν κίνησιν ἔχει
lexical_decisions.chosen: Does not water get its motion from wind
lexical_decisions.rationale: πνεῦμα can be wind or spirit. Wind fits the physical water-motion argument; the same word recurs as God’s Spirit in the quotation, preserving an important lexical link in these notes.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the origin of its movement
lexical_decisions.rationale: Here displacement or movement is intended, not religious ecstasy.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μετὰ τὸν ἀόρατον οὐρανὸν τὸν φαινόμενον ἐφαπλῶσαν
lexical_decisions.chosen: spreading out the visible heaven after the invisible one
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the visible/invisible distinction and after without supplying numbered heavens.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἢ γὰρ οὐχ ὑπὸ σιδήρου ἐτορνεύθησαν, — καὶ ὁ τορνεύσας σίδηρος ὑπὸ πυρὸς ἐμαλάχθη —
lexical_decisions.chosen: Were they not shaped on a lathe by iron—and was not the iron that shaped them on a lathe softened by fire—
lexical_decisions.rationale: Both forms of τορνεύω retain turning or lathe-working workmanship. Shaped alone is broader and would conceal the particular working image.

passages.text: For it was for you, the human being, that God commanded the water on the face of the earth to withdraw, so that the earth could offer you fruits. He made openings so that it might provide springs for you, streams of rivers might appear, and animals might be cast up. To put it briefly, so that everything could be at your service. Is it not for you that winds blow for the production of fruits, rains are brought, and seasonal turnings occur? Indeed, the sun and moon, together with the other stars, carry out their risings and settings for you, and rivers and lakes, together with all the springs, serve you. Therefore, just as greater honor was given to you, insensible though you are, so greater punishment through fire has been prepared for you in your ingratitude, because you were unwilling to know the one whom you ought to have known before all others.

lexical_decisions.chosen: He made openings
lexical_decisions.rationale: Bored holes or passages; no modern geological mechanism is specified.

lexical_decisions.chosen: and animals might be cast up
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the casting-up image, not generic creation.

lexical_decisions.chosen: and seasonal turnings occur
lexical_decisions.rationale: The turnings can concern the sun or seasons; the broader cyclical wording is retained.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ τρηδόνας ἐποίησεν, ἵνα σοι παράσχῃ πηγὰς
lexical_decisions.chosen: He made openings so that it might provide springs for you
lexical_decisions.rationale: It refers to the earth, the subject explicitly named in the preceding purpose clause and the bearer of the openings. The subject of παράσχῃ is unexpressed, so God, subject of made, remains a viable alternative: so that he might provide springs for you. The main text chooses earth without claiming the antecedent is uniquely settled.

passages.text: Even now, recognize from the lesser things the cause of all things, reasoning that water produces all things, that water receives the beginning of its motion from spirit, and that spirit has its origin from the God of all. This is how you ought to reason, so that through reason you may be able to reach God, in order that you may recognize your lineage, be born again through first-born water, and become an heir of the parents who begot you for incorruptibility.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τὸ δὲ ὕδωρ ὑπὸ πνεύματος κινήσεως τὴν γένεσιν λαμβάνει
lexical_decisions.chosen: water receives the beginning of its motion from spirit
lexical_decisions.rationale: Takes ὑπὸ πνεύματος together as the source of motion, with κινήσεως dependent on γένεσιν, beginning of motion. This agrees with the explicit water-motion argument in 11.22. Alternatively πνεύματος can depend on κινήσεως, with γένεσις as water’s coming into being: through the movement of spirit. Spirit can also be wind; both lexical senses remain possible, but no creation-from-nothing claim is added.

lexical_decisions.chosen: be born again through first-born water
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains the unusual birth-wording. Primordial water is a contextual alternative but would conceal the explicit birth epithet.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῶν πρὸς ἀφθαρσίαν γεννησάντων σε γονέων
lexical_decisions.chosen: the parents who begot you for incorruptibility
lexical_decisions.rationale: The source has plural parents and does not identify them in this clause; neither a singular parent nor specific identities are substituted.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἵνα ἐπὶ λόγῳ εἰς θεὸν καταντῆσαι δυνηθῇς, ὅπως ἐπιγνῶς σου τὸ γένος καὶ πρωτογόνῳ ἀναγεννηθῇς ὕδατι καὶ κληρονόμος καταστῇς τῶν πρὸς ἀφθαρσίαν γεννησάντων σε γονέων.
lexical_decisions.chosen: so that through reason you may be able to reach God, in order that you may recognize your lineage, be born again through first-born water, and become an heir of the parents who begot you for incorruptibility.
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains successive ἵνα and ὅπως purpose links: reasoning leads to reaching God, with recognition, rebirth, and inheritance introduced as the following purpose. The two links are not flattened into one list.

passages.text: Who does not see that it is better not to come together with a woman during her monthly condition, but after she has become clean and been immersed? And after intercourse one must also immerse oneself. If you shrink from doing this, recall how you pursued the parts of purity when you worshiped insensible idols. Be ashamed that here, where you ought to undertake not, I say, the greater part, but simply the whole of purity, you become more reluctant. So consider the one who made you act there, and you will understand who it is that puts reluctance toward purity into you here.

lexical_decisions.chosen: after she has become clean and been immersed
lexical_decisions.rationale: In this repeated purity setting βαπτίζω denotes bodily immersion; the same verb is baptized in the initiation setting. The contextual gloss difference does not claim different Greek words.

lexical_decisions.chosen: after intercourse one must also immerse oneself
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains repeated immersion after sexual intercourse, not mere inward purity or a newly asserted doctrine of repeated initiation.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οὐ τὸ πλεῖον λέγω, ἀλλὰ μόνον καὶ ὅλον τὸ τῆς ἁγνείας ἀναδέξασθαι
lexical_decisions.chosen: not, I say, the greater part, but simply the whole of purity
lexical_decisions.rationale: The preceding parts (μέρη) and following whole (ὅλον) support a quantitative greater-part/whole contrast. More is another viable rendering of τὸ πλεῖον. Simply treats μόνον adverbially, while whole retains ὅλον; the phrase is not made into an unspecified greater thing.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: νοήσατε οὖν τὸν ἐκεῖ ὑμᾶς πεποιηκότα
lexical_decisions.chosen: So consider the one who made you act there
lexical_decisions.rationale: Act is an inferred complement from the preceding account of pursuing purity, not restored missing wording. The more literal the one who made you there, understood as making or forming them as they were, remains an alternative. The behavioral reading is preferred because the following clause concerns the one inducing current reluctance; neither unnamed agent is independently identified.

passages.text: No: rather, do more, so that if those in error do not murder, we do not even become angry; if the person in error does not commit adultery, we do not even think of it in the first place; if the person in error loves the one who loves him, we also love those who hate us; if the person in error lends to those who have, we also lend to those who do not have. In short, we who hope to inherit the boundless age ought to do better than the good things done by those who know only the present age. We know that if their deeds, examined alongside our deeds on the day of judgment, are found equal in doing good, we too must be put to shame, while they, through error having done what is against them, must perish. I spoke of being put to shame in this respect: we did not do more than they did, although we also knew more than they did. But if we are to be put to shame for displaying good deeds equal to theirs and not more, how much more if we display less good conduct than theirs?

lexical_decisions.source_quote: οἱ τὸν ἄπειρον αἰῶνα ἐλπίζοντες κληρονομεῖν
lexical_decisions.chosen: we who hope to inherit the boundless age
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἄπειρος means boundless or endless; αἰών remains age, contrasting the present age.

lexical_decisions.chosen: we also knew more than they did
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὧν is the comparative genitive supplying the comparison for πλεῖον ἐγνώκαμεν, not an object meaning knowledge about those people. Although in the main sentence makes the contextual contrast of greater knowledge but insufficient greater deeds readable; it is not a new independent fact.

passages.text: That on the day of judgment the actions of those who have known the truth are indeed measured against the good deeds of those who have been deceived, the one who does not lie himself taught us ...., saying to those who neglected to come and listen to him, “The queen of the south will rise with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom; and look, something greater than Solomon is here, and you do not believe.” To those among the people who were unwilling to reorient at his proclamation, he said, “Men of Nineveh will rise with this generation and condemn it, because on hearing they reoriented in response to Jonah’s proclamation; and look, something greater ... is here, and no one believes.” Thus, setting over against each of their acts of impiety those from the nations who had acted, to condemn those in reverence toward God who had not done even as much good as those who had been deceived, he admonished those with understanding not merely to do good things equally with the nations, but to do more. My discourse flowed on, taking its starting point from the need to observe menstrual separation and to immerse oneself after intercourse: not to reject such purity even if those who have been deceived practice it, since those in error who do good serve to condemn those in reverence toward God, although they themselves are not saved. For their honoring of purity is because of error, not because of worship of the true Father and God of all.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the one who does not lie himself taught us ....
lexical_decisions.rationale: The selected edition has four gap dots; exactly four remain, without reconstruction.

lexical_decisions.chosen: and look, something greater ... is here
lexical_decisions.rationale: Exactly three gap dots remain. No familiar proper name from another witness is supplied.

lexical_decisions.chosen: they reoriented in response to Jonah’s proclamation
lexical_decisions.rationale: Uses POB reorientation terminology, traditionally repented, preserving the stated occasion of the response.

lexical_decisions.chosen: although they themselves are not saved
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the author’s explicit non-salvation claim about people in error who nonetheless do good.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to observe menstrual separation
lexical_decisions.rationale: The purity context concerns observance of menstrual separation, not merely monitoring a cycle. The menstrual period is a viable temporal rendering; if the noun is taken personally, the menstruating woman is another possible referent. The main text selects the separation observance.

lexical_decisions.chosen: their honoring of purity
lexical_decisions.rationale: The context of people practicing purity supports τιμή as their valuing or honoring the practice, with αὐτῶν related to that honoring. The esteem or value of their purity, attaching αὐτῶν to ἁγνείας, is a material alternative and is not excluded by the main rendering.

source_issues.issue: Exactly 4 printed gap dots remain in the English; no unavailable words are restored.
Exactly 3 printed gap dots remain in the English; no unavailable words are restored.

The selected edition supplies an isolated dot before τῆς. English reads the phrase with this generation across that punctuation. This single dot is distinguished from the section’s four-dot and three-dot printed gaps; it is not called an OCR error and no replacement Greek is proposed.

passages.text: When three months had been completed, he instructed me to fast for days, led me to the nearby springs in the sea, and baptized me as into ever-flowing water. After our brothers had thus feasted at my God-given rebirth, not many days later he turned to the elders before the whole assembly and gave these instructions: “Our Lord and prophet, who sent us, explained to us how the evil one conversed with him for forty days and, having gained no power against him, promised to send apostles from among his own subjects to deceive. Therefore, above all, remember not to ... an apostle or teacher or prophet before he has compared his proclamation with James, who is called the brother of my Lord and has been entrusted in Jerusalem with administering the assembly of the Hebrews, and has come to you with witnesses. This is so that the evil that conversed with the Lord for forty days and gained no power, and afterward fell like lightning from heaven to earth, may not send out a herald against you, as it has now put Simon in our way, proclaiming in the name of your Lord under the pretext of truth, but sowing error. For this reason the one who sent us said, ‘Many will come to me in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravenous wolves; recognize them by their fruits.’”

lexical_decisions.chosen: he instructed me to fast for days
lexical_decisions.rationale: The supplied wording gives days but no explicit number; none is restored.

lexical_decisions.chosen: baptized me as into ever-flowing water
lexical_decisions.rationale: ὡς qualifies the into-ever-flowing-water phrase and characterizes the baptism/water in this way. An alternative construal is that the springs provided water treated as continuously flowing. The wording does not assert that the water was only apparently flowing.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: μὴ πρότερον . . . ἀντιβάλλοντα αὐτοῦ τὸ κήρυγμα Ἰακώβῳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: not to ... an apostle or teacher or prophet before he has compared his proclamation with James
lexical_decisions.rationale: Exactly three dots remain. The governing action is unavailable and is not supplied as receive or trust. The negative/before relation, comparison of proclamation, and subsequent witnesses remain.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the brother of my Lord
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps my here and your Lord later rather than harmonizing pronouns.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: πολλοὶ ἐλεύσονται πρὸς μὲ ἐν ἐνδύματι προβάτων
lexical_decisions.chosen: Many will come to me in sheep’s clothing
lexical_decisions.rationale: Keeps the supplied to me, rather than importing a familiar to you from another witness.

source_issues.issue: The three-dot gap leaves the governing action unavailable. Exactly three dots remain, with the negative, temporal relation, proclamation comparison and witnesses preserved rather than reconstruction from another witness.

The supplied edition has a question mark after days. It is recorded as a print/editorial feature without claiming its purpose is known; the surviving phrase is rendered for forty days, not made into an English question. This is distinct from the disclosed three-dot lacuna elsewhere in the section.

passages.text: After saying these things, he sent the advance party to Antioch in Syria, telling them to wait there the following day. After they had gone, Peter drove away diseases, afflictions, and demons from large crowds who had been persuaded, baptized them in the nearby springs in the sea, and broke the Eucharist. He appointed Maron, who had received him and was by now mature, as overseer, designated twelve elders, appointed attendants, and organized arrangements for widows. He addressed the constituted body concerning the common or beneficial interest of the assembly and advised them to obey Maron the overseer. Since three months had now been completed, he took leave of those in Tripolis in Phoenicia and set out on the road to Antioch in Syria, with everyone accompanying us on our way with the appropriate honor.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to wait there the following day
lexical_decisions.rationale: The following is understood with the ordinary elliptical day; no exact date is supplied.

lexical_decisions.chosen: broke the Eucharist
lexical_decisions.rationale: The source combines breaking with Eucharist/thanksgiving, implicitly its bread. The breaking action is retained rather than merely offered thanks.

lexical_decisions.chosen: overseer
lexical_decisions.rationale: Translates the office’s sense; bishop is the conventional title alternative.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: καὶ διακόνους δείξας καὶ χηρικὰ συστησάμενος
lexical_decisions.chosen: appointed attendants, and organized arrangements for widows
lexical_decisions.rationale: διάκονοι can be attendants or deacons. χηρικά means matters/institutions for widows, not an invented beneficiary list.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὑπέρ τε τοῦ κοινοῦ ἢ συμφέροντος τῆς ἐκκλησίας
lexical_decisions.chosen: concerning the common or beneficial interest of the assembly
lexical_decisions.rationale: The interest phrase qualifies Peter’s speaking, not a property added to the order. Concerning is a topical rendering of ὑπέρ; for the benefit of gives its purposive alternative. The printed or (ἢ) remains rather than being silently changed to and.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὑπέρ τε τοῦ κοινοῦ ἢ συμφέροντος τῆς ἐκκλησίας τὴν τάξιν προσομιλήσας
lexical_decisions.chosen: He addressed the constituted body concerning the common or beneficial interest of the assembly
lexical_decisions.rationale: τάξις is understood as the constituted body or order being addressed, in context after institutional appointments. Speaking about organizational arrangements is a material alternative. The chosen interpretation gives the body as recipient while attaching the common/beneficial concern to the address, not inventing a that-served relative clause.
